messages:
maya: quick share — ran a targeted bench comparing streaming endpoints (SSE, websocket) vs sync/batched HTTP polling across GPUs/regions. attached charts show p50/p99 and aggregate token throughput. TL;DR: streaming gives much better p50 for interactive UX, but non-streaming batch > streaming on tokens/sec under high concurrency due to batch fusion on H100.

devon: can you drop the raw numbers + config? curious about seq len and batch sizes.

maya: sure — test harness: 
```
concurrency: 200
avg_input_tokens: 64
max_output_tokens: 128
streaming: [sse, websocket, http-poll]
batch_windows: [0ms, 20ms, 50ms]
gpus: [A100-80GB, H100-80GB]
region: [us-west1, eu-west1]
metrics: p50_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, connections
```
result snapshot (p50 / p99 / tok/s):
```
us-west1 A100  | SSE   18ms / 240ms  | 28k tok/s
us-west1 A100  | WS    20ms / 260ms  | 26k tok/s
us-west1 A100  | HTTP  45ms / 480ms  | 60k tok/s (batched)
eu-west1 H100   | SSE   15ms / 220ms  | 34k tok/s
eu-west1 H100   | WS    16ms / 230ms  | 33k tok/s
eu-west1 H100   | HTTP  38ms / 420ms  | 78k tok/s (batched, fused kernel)
```
Note: HTTP numbers assume 20ms batching window + dynamic batching. SSE/WS had lower p50 but per-connection fanout reduced aggregate throughput.

liam: nice. which kernel paths did you force for H100? flash-attn or fused multihead? any tf32 vs fp16 differences?

maya: we let runtime pick kernels but pinned a fused-kernel path on H100 for long sequences (>=128). flash-attn-v2 on A100 gave best latency for short seq. tf32 gave comparable perf for fp16 on H100 for our workload, but int8/4bit quant gave ~1.7-1.9x tokens/sec uplift with negligible eval-regression on our small rubric (still running larger evals).

nina: region differences — was network fanout the main reason SSE throughput dropped vs HTTP?

maya: yes — SSE/WS keep connections hot so the per-connection dispatch + prefix cache misses across shards add overhead when you have high fanout. eu-west1 had higher baseline GPU capability (H100 pools) so it offset some of that overhead and showed higher tok/s even for SSE.

devon: repro command? I'd like to run on staging.

maya: repro gist: https://redwood.internal/bench/gists/1719876543 (dashboard + raw csv attached). quick cmd: `./bench --mode=sse --concurrency=200 --seq=64 --model=redwood/open-13b-quant --region=eu-west1 --gpu=h100`

ops: note — autoscaler behaves poorly with long-lived streaming connections right now. streaming ties up pods; we saw spike where autoscaler didn't reclaim fast enough and dedicated pool exhausted. filed infra ticket #INF-472.

bench-bot: summary: 8 runs, median p50 delta (SSE vs HTTP-batch) = -22ms (SSE faster), aggregate tok/s delta = -35% (SSE lower). attached CSV: s3://bench-results/1719876543.csv

liam: proposed next steps: (1) run quantized model with HTTP batch windows 10/20/50ms to map knee; (2) experiment with ephemeral fanout proxies to reduce per-connection cost for SSE; (3) extended eval on quality for int4 to be safe.

maya: agree. I'll kick off batch of repros for int8/int4 + batch-window sweep and post back in this thread. tagging @ops for autoscaler follow-up. thanks all :rocket:
